raw_response:
I’m 60 this year, and I’ve farmed these fields a long time, so I won’t do anything too risky. On my land, wheat and maize are still the backbone because they are steady, and with the well I can protect yield in a dry spell. But cash is not loose and there are only two of us at home, so I won’t chase very high input. I’ll keep most of the land in the usual wheat-maize rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton. The extension man says rates more exact than before, but in practice I still look at last year’s crop color, the soil moisture, and what the neighbors are doing. If wheat looks weak after winter, I add a bit more topdressing; if rain comes in time, I save one irrigation for maize.

For this year, I plan to put about 7.0 mu into wheat-maize double cropping and 3.1 mu into cotton. Wheat and maize turn over very tight, so after wheat harvest I won’t do heavy tillage, just quick residue clearing and shallow rotary tillage so maize can go in on time. Cotton takes more watching and more hand work, so I keep it smaller. I’d rather spend a bit more on wheat and maize fertilizer than let yield fall too much, but I still keep some cash in hand in case pumping, pests, or family needs come up.
